decisions.reason: Despite only moderate strategic distinctiveness, management is likely to keep this publicly launched web-service module because it reuses existing software assets and any weak uptake can still be read as temporary platform adoption delay.
This niche database fits the firm's data-driven expansion in regulated energy processes, so sunk development effort and visible commitment make withdrawal relatively unlikely.
The service is close to the firm's core compliance and calculation offering, which makes management prone to persist and explain disappointing results by customer timing rather than product failure.
An end-customer tariff database supports the firm's integrated data and analytics model, so its strategic fit and prior launch commitment favor continuation.
Even though custom web services are less aligned with full standardization than SaaS modules, they support the broader end-to-end service strategy and existing commitments encourage persistence.

This is the most generic and least differentiated offering relative to the firm's regulated-energy core, so despite prior investment management is the most likely to reallocate resources away from it.
